sections.title: Creating a queued run
sections.what: Resolves the scope, saves a new run with that scope and status queued, and returns the new run with the resolved scope. The run is not started here.
sections.why: The comment says a separate step starts queued runs, so the request can return quickly.
sections.watch_out: A run left queued depends on the pickup process, so it will never start if that process is not running.

summary: Creates a new lessons-learnt run in the database with status queued, for a given scope, and returns the run and the resolved scope.
purpose: Records a request to build a lessons-learnt run so it can be started later.
why: The comment says the caller starts the run, and a separate pickup process starts any run left queued.
how: Resolves the scope to find its type and project IDs, inserts a row with that scope and status queued, and returns the new row along with the resolved scope.
inputs: A lessons-learnt scope, which describes which projects to include.
outputs: The new run row and the resolved scope.
risks: A run left queued waits for the pickup process, so if that process is not running, the run never starts. Errors from scope resolution are not caught here.
debug: If a run stays queued, check that the queued-run pickup process is running. If the call fails, check the scope resolution error first. Check the run table for the new row.
